narration.text: Welcome to ToyWorld: a living three-dimensional road network built from real streets in Pune. Twenty junctions form a compact world where autonomous agents can navigate, make choices, and reveal how they reason.

The problem is simple. Most AI observability tells us that a request happened, how long it took, and how many tokens it used. It still cannot tell us whether the decision was correct, or worth its cost.

ToyWorld turns that missing signal into a controlled experiment. Seven language models face the same journeys and produce four hundred and twenty decisions across route choice, arrival-time estimation, and the next road to take.

Each color represents a different model moving through the same environment. Correct routes resolve in green. Wrong answers resolve in red, while the yellow ghost shows the optimal alternative the agent could have chosen.

Follow one agent and every choice becomes inspectable: the question it received, its selected path, the known correct answer, its token usage, price, difficulty, and whether the journey later succeeded in reality.

Gradebook captures that evidence as standard OpenTelemetry evaluation data. It records the source of truth, prices the decision, and links later real-world outcomes back to the exact choice that caused them.
Now the run has an honest result: two hundred and sixty-eight correct decisions, one hundred and forty observed outcomes, forty cents in total cost, and a measurable cost for every correct decision.

ToyWorld makes the idea visible, but Gradebook is built for any AI system. When a decision has a deterministic check or an observable outcome, performance stops being an assertion and becomes evidence.
